about: Analytic-redundancy rules: pairs of readings that must agree with each other, instead of each being judged against a fixed range. A rule runs only when every side and every condition channel was read at the same moment (max_skew_s). 'basis' says why the two must agree: 'physics', a citation already in this repo, or 'heuristic, adjustable'. 'tolerance_basis' says where the tolerance number comes from. Edit the numbers here to adjust them; nothing else needs changing. Side keys: 'channel' (cuore.live.channels id), 'channel.part' (one field of a multi-part value), 'channel@18DAF1xx' (that module's own answer to the PID; only present in saved pids_snapshot observations).

rules.title: MAP vs barometric pressure, engine off
rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (both PIDs are whole kPa)
rules.basis: physics: with the engine stopped the intake manifold is open to the atmosphere, so MAP equals barometric pressure

rules.title: Barometric pressure: PID 33 vs ECM DID 1956
rules.basis: physics: two readings of the one atmospheric pressure. Repo citation: cuore/live/did_catalog.py, ECM 0x1956 ('barometric PID 100 kPa agrees')

rules.title: Absolute boost (DID 195A) vs barometric pressure, engine off
rules.basis: physics: an absolute pressure sensor in the intake reads atmospheric pressure with the engine stopped. Repo citation: the 0x195A decoding bug of 2026-10-25 (cuore/services/sensor_health.py FORMULA_FIX_AT) is exactly what this catches

rules.title: Absolute boost (DID 195A) vs ambient pressure (DID 1956), engine off
rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable. Repo evidence: 1001 vs 1004 mbar and MES 988 vs 990 mbar (cuore/live/did_catalog.py notes)
rules.basis: physics: engine stopped, both DIDs are the same atmospheric pressure

rules.title: Absolute boost (DID 195A) vs MAP, throttle wide open
rules.basis: heuristic, adjustable: with the throttle wide open the charge pipe and the manifold should be at the same pressure (engineering inference, not a repo citation). NOT checked at idle: this car's own readings show they differ there (2026-10-13 20:38, idle 734 rpm: DID 195A 98.2 kPa = ambient, MAP 32 kPa), consistent with the boost sensor sitting upstream of a closed throttle

rules.title: Coolant temperature: ECM vs TCM answer to PID 05
rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (2026-10-26: 64 vs 63 C; 2026-10-14: 72 vs 71 C)
rules.basis: heuristic, adjustable: both modules report the car's coolant temperature; they may filter or sample it differently

rules.title: Coolant temperature: PID 05 vs ECM DID 1003
rules.basis: physics: the same coolant temperature read two ways. DID 1003 decoding is unverified on the 2.0T (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Coolant vs ambient air, after a long cold soak

conditions.text: engine off for at least 6 h (stated by you, not readable from the car)

rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (sun, wind and bumper-mounted ambient sensors add error)
rules.basis: physics: after hours with the engine off, every fluid and air temperature relaxes to ambient

rules.title: Coolant vs engine oil temperature, after a long cold soak

conditions.text: engine off for at least 6 h (stated by you, not readable from the car)

rules.basis: physics: after hours with the engine off, oil and coolant reach the same temperature. DID 1302 decoding is unverified (single byte, cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Coolant vs intake air (sensor 1), after a long cold soak

conditions.text: engine off for at least 6 h (stated by you, not readable from the car)

rules.basis: physics: after hours with the engine off, intake air relaxes to the same temperature as the coolant

rules.title: Intake air (sensor 1) vs ambient air, after a long cold soak

conditions.text: engine off for at least 6 h (stated by you, not readable from the car)

rules.basis: physics: after hours with the engine off, intake air relaxes to ambient

rules.title: Coolant vs gearbox oil temperature, after a long cold soak

conditions.text: engine off for at least 6 h (stated by you, not readable from the car)

rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (the gearbox cools differently from the engine)
rules.basis: physics: after hours with the engine off, gearbox oil relaxes to ambient like the coolant. DID 04FE decoding is unverified on the 2.0T (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Battery voltage: adapter (ATRV) vs ECM control-module voltage (PID 42)

sides.label: Battery at the OBD port (adapter ATRV)

rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (ATRV is a coarse ADC and sees cable drop)
rules.basis: physics: one battery, measured at two points of the same 12 V supply. Repo citation: cuore/live/channels.py load_step_voltage preset (ATRV 14.5 V vs BCM 14.5 V on 2026-10-23)

rules.title: Battery voltage: adapter (ATRV) vs BCM DID 1004

sides.label: Battery at the OBD port (adapter ATRV)

rules.basis: physics: one battery. Repo citation: cuore/live/channels.py load_step_voltage preset (ATRV 14.5 V vs BCM 14.5 V on 2026-10-23). DID 1004 formula A/10 is unverified

rules.title: Vehicle speed: PID 0D vs ECM DID 1002
rules.basis: physics: one road speed read two ways. DID 1002 decoding is unverified on the 2.0T (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Engine speed: PID 0C vs ECM DID 1000
rules.tolerance_basis: heuristic, adjustable (idle RPM wanders by tens of rpm between two reads)
rules.basis: physics: one crankshaft speed read two ways. DID 1000 is unverified on the 2.0T (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Throttle position: PID 11 vs PID 47
rules.basis: heuristic, adjustable: the two throttle tracks measure one plate and should follow each other

rules.title: Accelerator pedal: PID 49 vs PID 4A
rules.basis: heuristic, adjustable: redundant pedal tracks report the one pedal position

rules.title: Fuel level: PID 2F vs ECM DID 1001
rules.basis: physics: one tank level read two ways. DID 1001 is unverified on the 2.0T (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

rules.title: Engine run time: PID 1F vs ECM DID 1009
rules.basis: heuristic, adjustable: both count time since the engine started. DID 1009 decoding is unverified (cuore/live/did_catalog.py)

needs.title: Wheel speeds against each other and against vehicle speed
needs.needs: ABS wheel-speed channels FL, FR, RL, RR
needs.why: No ABS wheel-speed channel exists in cuore/live/channels.py (DID_MODULES is ECM, TCM, BCM, IPC, RFHUB only).
needs.basis: physics: on a straight, steady drive the four wheel speeds equal each other and the vehicle speed within tyre-radius differences

needs.title: Throttle: commanded vs actual
needs.why: The decoder in cuore/live/obd.py has actual throttle (PID 11, 47) and pedal (49, 4A) but no commanded-throttle PID.
needs.basis: physics: a healthy throttle body follows its command

needs.title: EVAP purge: commanded vs actual flow
needs.needs: a measured purge-flow or ESIM channel
needs.why: PID 2E is the commanded purge only. 'esim_status' has no readable DID, and the ESIM probe channels need hardware on CUORE_ESIM_PROBE_PORT.
needs.basis: physics: commanded purge duty should move manifold pressure and fuel trim

needs.title: Fuel trims against purge duty
needs.needs: a purge on/off transition, not a single moment
needs.why: The channels exist (commanded_evap_purge, short_fuel_trim_b1, long_fuel_trim_b1) but the expected relation is a change over time, handled by cuore/live/purge_trim.py, not by a same-moment agreement.

needs.title: Battery voltage: IBS (battery sensor) vs adapter
needs.needs: a decoded voltage field from BCM DID 1005 (IBS composite)
needs.why: bcm_1005 has only a prose description, no machine-readable formula (cuore/live/channels.py treats 'multi-field' as undecoded).

needs.title: Battery voltage: ECM DID 1955
needs.why: It answered requestOutOfRange (NRC 31) on this car on 2026-10-23 (cuore/live/channels.py, load_step_voltage comment).

needs.title: Boost sensor raw voltage (DID 195B) vs boost pressure (195A)
needs.needs: the boost sensor's voltage-to-pressure transfer function
needs.why: 195B is an unconfirmed decoding (reads about 0.03 V while the module answers; cuore/services/sensor_health.py flags it) and no transfer function is on record.
needs.basis: physics: the sensor output voltage is a fixed function of its pressure

needs.title: Throttle sensors 2 and 3 (DIDs 1925, 1926) against sensor 1
needs.why: They are not percent (likely degrees); cuore/services/sensor_health.py suspect_reason says they are not comparable with throttle position in %.
